g.text: 93% of records sit in urban centres, home to 34% of people; in the sparsest areas (15% of

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 17px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: people) only 36% are within an hour of confirmed trauma care, against 86% in urban centres

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: Settlement class: simplified Degree of Urbanisation (GHSL/Eurostat thresholds, no gap filling) on WorldPop 2025 1 km cells; it counts dense villages of the Gangetic plain as

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: towns, so its rural share is smaller than the Census 2011 rural share (68.8%). Records are placed by cleaned location; a record geocoded to its town centre counts as urban.

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: Confirmed = dataset claim plus a second check, mostly the own website (see s6). Population classes are modelled, so no sampling interval applies; travel error range in s4.
